description: Utilizing the old Court Complex Buildings located in the Galle Fort for a Tourism Promotion Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-04-06 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Galle Fort, which has been declared as a World Heritage Site by the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO), attracts over 300,000 local and foreign tourists every year to visit and spend their leisure time there. However, due to the fact that some roads in the Galle Fort, where a large number of buildings are located and which are used for administrative/institutional purposes, are congested during the day and become isolated at night, tourists have had to encounter various obstacles in using the area. Galle Fort has been declared a World Heritage Tourism Zone under the Development Plan for Greater Galle Area (2021-2030). Also, the Urban Development Authority has planned an integrated development programme called the 'Galle Revival Project' to conserve the buildings of archaeological value in the Galle Fort and utilize them for tourism purposes. The proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to establish the High Court and Magistrate's Court, which are currently housed in the Galle Fort, in the new Court Complex constructed in the Beligaha area of ​​Galle under the said programme, and to hand over those buildings to the Urban Development Authority to implement a tourism promotion project under the Public Private Partnership method, was approved by the Cabinet.
